intro: Routes, flights and ships, kinds of accommodation and the mishaps of a long trip.
p.itinerario.consejo: It is masculine: «el itinerario». It ends in an unstressed «-io»: «i-ti-ne-RA-ryo».
p.trayecto.consejo: A long journey can have several trayectos. The «y» sounds as in «yo»: «tra-YEK-to».
p.recorrer.consejo: The «rr» is strong: «rre-ko-RRER». You «recorres» a whole country; you do not just cross it.
p.atravesar.consejo: The e changes: «atravieso», «atraviesas». You cross a river, a country or an ocean.
p.escala.consejo: You say «hacer escala»: «el vuelo hace escala en Lisboa». With no stops, it is «directo».
p.embarcar.consejo: Before «e» the c becomes «qu»: «embarque». The opposite is «desembarcar».
p.tripulación.consejo: It ends in «-ción»: «tri-pu-la-THYON». It looks after the passengers during the trip.
p.aduana.consejo: You «pasas» through customs and «declaras» what you carry. The u sounds: «a-DWA-na».
p.extraviar.consejo: It is more formal than «perder»: «me han extraviado la maleta».
p.albergue.consejo: In «-gue» the u is silent and the g is hard: «al-BER-ge», like «get».
p.acampar.consejo: It comes from «campo». Before «e» the c becomes «qu»: «acampe».
p.tienda de campaña.consejo: A «tienda» is also a shop. «De campaña» makes clear it is for the countryside.
p.alojarse.consejo: The j sounds h: «a-lo-HAR-se». You «te alojas» «en» a hotel or hostel.
p.dar la vuelta al mundo.consejo: It is also used figuratively. «La vuelta al mundo en ochenta días» is a famous novel.
b1.texto:
**The route.** **El itinerario** is the travel plan and **el trayecto**, each part. You **recorres** a whole country and **atraviesas** a river, a desert or an ocean. Some people want to **dar la vuelta al mundo**.

**By plane and by ship.** A flight can be **directo** or **hacer escala**. Passengers **embarcan** and **la tripulación** looks after them.

**At customs.** You go through **la aduana** and declare what you carry. If they **extravían** your suitcase, you claim it at the airport desk.

**Where to sleep.** **Un hotel**, **un albergue** (cheap and shared), **un parador**, **una casa rural**. Or you **acampas** and put up **la tienda de campaña**. Useful verb: **alojarse en**.
b2.f0.texto: They have lost my suitcase at the stopover in Lisbon.
b2.f2.texto: We left Madrid, stopped over in Lisbon and arrived in Prague.
b2.f3.texto: Fill in this form and describe your suitcase.
b2.f5.texto: We will call the customs office in Prague to look for it.
b2.f6.texto: Tonight I am staying at a hostel near the airport.
b2.f7.texto: If the suitcase turns up, we will let you know by phone.
b4.titulo: I am looking for a place that has…
b4.texto:
When you talk about something you **know**, the verb of the relative clause is **indicative**: **conozco un albergue que tiene cocina**.

When you talk about something you **do not know exists**, it is **subjunctive**: **busco un albergue que tenga cocina**.

In the past it works the same way, with the imperfect subjunctive: **buscaba un barco que admitiera pasajeros** (he did not know whether it existed).

The question is always the same: does it already exist, or am I looking for it?
b4.e0.texto: I am looking for a hostel that has a kitchen.
b4.e1.texto: I know a hostel that has a kitchen.
b4.e2.texto: He was looking for a ship that would take passengers.
b5.f0.texto: Ignacio crosses the harbour at dawn with a worn backpack over his shoulder.
b5.f1.texto: The itinerary, folded a thousand times, trembles between his fingers like a bird.
b5.f2.texto: On the quay, the crew of the ship greets him with hoarse voices.
b5.f3.texto: The air on the quay tastes of salt and hot oil.
b5.f4.texto: He boards without looking back because he knows the journey has already begun.
b5.f5.texto: For weeks the sea is a grey plain without a single coast.
b5.f6.texto: At night Ignacio sleeps in a narrow cabin that vibrates with the engine.
b5.f7.texto: At the stopover in Lisbon, a seller offers him hot chestnuts.
b5.f8.texto: At customs they check his backpack and look with suspicion at his tent.
b5.f9.texto: When he finally camps beside a river, Ignacio stays looking at the stars.
b6.o0.refuerzo: The escala is about a stop, not how many people travel.
b6.o1: un vuelo que para en otro sitio
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes: the plane makes a stop before reaching the final destination.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Directo is the opposite: it makes no stop.
b6.pregunta: What does «un vuelo con escala» mean?
b7.o0.refuerzo: It is indicative: it is for a ship you already know.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It is future, but the story is told in the past.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Yes: past tense and an unknown ship need the imperfect subjunctive.
b7.pregunta: Which form goes if you do not know the ship exists?
b8.frase: Recorrimos el país de norte a sur
b8.traduccion: We travelled the country from north to south
b9.o0.refuerzo: Yes: it is the cloth shelter for sleeping in the countryside.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The tripulación is the people who work on a ship or plane.
b9.o2.refuerzo: The itinerario is the trip plan, not something to sleep in.
b9.pregunta: What do you take for camping?
b11.frase: Me han ____ la maleta en el aeropuerto.
b11.o0.refuerzo: Acampar is sleeping in a tent; it does not apply to a suitcase.
b11.o1.refuerzo: Yes: extraviar is losing something without knowing where it is.
b11.o2.refuerzo: Recorrer is travelling around a place; you do not do it to a suitcase.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Embarcar is getting on a ship or a plane.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Atravesar is crossing from one side to the other, not seeing the whole country.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Yes: recorrer is travelling all over a place.
b12.pregunta: You travel all over a country. Which verb do you use?
p.extraviado.consejo: «extraviado» means lost. It comes from «extraviar», to mislay.
p.hicimos.consejo: «hacer» has an irregular past: «hicimos». The «h» is silent.
p.llegamos.consejo: «llegar» means to arrive. The «g» before «a» is hard: ye-GA-mos.
p.describa.consejo: «describa» is the polite command form for «usted». The «c» before «r» is «k».
p.llevaba.consejo: The imperfect «llevaba» describes an action in the past that continued. The «ll» is «y».
p.llamaremos.consejo: The future «llamaremos» has the stress on «RE». The «ll» is «y».
p.buscarla.consejo: «la» refers to a feminine noun, such as «la maleta». «buscarla» means to look for it.
p.alojo.consejo: «alojarse» means to stay somewhere. The «j» sounds like «h»: a-LO-ho.
p.tenga.consejo: «tenga» appears after «que» when we are looking for something. The «g» is hard.
p.admitiera.consejo: The «ie» diphthong is one sound in «admitiera». It follows an imagined situation.
p.pasajeros.consejo: «pasajero» is masculine: «el pasajero». The «j» is a strong «h».
p.gastada.consejo: «gastada» agrees with «mochila», feminine. It comes from «gastar».
p.doblado.consejo: «doblado» means folded. The «v» sound in «doblar» is «b».
p.muelle.consejo: «muelle» is masculine: «el muelle». The «ue» is one sound and the «ll» is «y».
p.embarca.consejo: «embarcar» means to board a ship or plane. The «c» before «a» sounds «k».
p.atrás.consejo: «atrás» means backwards. The accent marks the last syllable: a-TRAS.
p.empezado.consejo: «empezado» is the past participle of «empezar». Here it means it has already begun.
p.noches.consejo: «noche» is feminine: «la noche». The «ch» sounds as in «church».
p.camarote.consejo: «camarote» is masculine: «el camarote». The stress is on «RO».
p.desconfianza.consejo: «desconfianza» is feminine: «la desconfianza». The prefix «des-» means lack of.
p.acampa.consejo: «acampar» means to camp outdoors. The «c» before «a» sounds «k».
p.recorrimos.consejo: «recorrer» means to travel across. The «rr» in the middle is strong.
